_about: Model configuration for the workshop, committed so nobody has to edit their
home directory. Keys beginning with _ are notes: pi ignores unknown keys.
Sampling values are cited. Where we deviate from a vendor recommendation the
reason is recorded, because an unexplained sampling value is impossible for
anyone else to reason about later.

local.name: Local llamafile
_note: apiKey is a placeholder: llamafile ignores it, but pi requires a model to
have auth before it appears in /model, so it must be non-empty.
compat: llamafile does not understand the `developer` role or
reasoning_effort, so both are turned off.

models.name: Bonsai 8B Q1_0 (llamafile)
_note: contextWindow is 16384, well under the model's native 65536, and it MUST
equal the server's -c value or pi's reply allowance collapses and the
agent silently returns nothing. Measured: a 65536 window needs ~10 GiB
of RAM, since this model spends 144 KiB of KV cache per token.
Sampling per the official model card (Temperature 0.5, range 0.5-0.7;
Top-k 20, range 20-40; Top-p 0.9, range 0.85-0.95; Repetition penalty
1.0), EXCEPT temperature, which we set to 0.2 deliberately: the task is
reporting findings from a tool, not writing prose, and an A/B at 0.6 on
25 real messages showed no improvement and introduced new garbles.
min_p is stated explicitly as 0. The card does not mention it, and
leaving it out does NOT mean it is off: llama.cpp defaults min_p to
0.05 (common/common.h), so the card's configuration is only actually
in effect once this is said out loud.

models.name: Granite 4.1 3B Q6_K (llamafile)
_note: IBM's card documents 131072 context, Apache 2.0, and explicitly lists
tool calling among the model's capabilities.
SAMPLING: IBM publishes no prose recommendation, but their declared
default is GREEDY, and that is what we use. Evidence:
generation_config.json for ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b contains only
bos/eos/pad token ids and transformers_version -- no do_sample, no
temperature, no top_p, no top_k -- and every official example calls
generate() with no sampling arguments, which in transformers means
do_sample=False. Unsloth's Granite 4.1 page independently lists
temperature 0.0, top_k 0, top_p 1.0.
Greedy is also right for this task: the model reports facts a tool has
already computed, so sampling buys nothing, and it makes the workshop
reproducible -- everyone gets the same output from the same message.
min_p is stated explicitly because llama.cpp defaults it to 0.05
(common/common.h: `float min_p = 0.05f;`), an active truncation
sampler. Setting temperature and top_p while leaving min_p unstated
leaves a sampler running that nobody chose.
The Unsloth GGUF card says to pass --jinja to llama.cpp. llamafile
0.10.5 enables it by default (`--jinja, --no-jinja ... default:
enabled`), so nothing extra is needed here; on an older llama.cpp build
you would have to add it or tool calling may not work.
KV cache is 80 KiB per token (40 layers x 8 KV heads x 64 head_dim x
2 bytes, doubled for K and V = 81920 bytes), so a full 131072 window
needs ~10 GiB. 16384 is the workshop setting; raise -c and
contextWindow together if you raise it at all.

hosted.name: Hosted endpoint (contingency)
_note: PLACEHOLDER — not usable until baseUrl is filled in.
A fallback for anyone whose machine is too slow to run the model locally.
Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving one of these GGUFs works; a Hugging
Face Inference Endpoint running llama.cpp is the obvious choice, since it
is the same server the local llamafile runs.
To use it:
1. Replace REPLACE-ME below with the endpoint host.
2. export HF_TOKEN=hf_...    (the token is read from the environment and
never stored in this file — do not paste it here, it would be
committed.)
3. WORKSHOP_PROVIDER=hosted WORKSHOP_MODEL=<id> ./pi-workshop.sh
Check the endpoint before relying on it, because both matter:
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" <host>/props \
| grep -o '"n_ctx":[0-9]*'                  # must match contextWindow
... | grep -o '"supports_tools":[a-z]*'       # must be true, or the
# extension's tool is
# never called
A hosted endpoint scaled to zero returns HTTP 503 until it wakes, which
takes a minute or two. That is not a misconfiguration; retry.
